Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity discovery recap - SummitData

Alex - thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call so we have a shared record and clear next steps. Let me know if I missed anything or if you'd prefer this in a Google Doc.

Key pain points you shared:
- Unpredictable inference latency on bursty nightly workloads (billing spikes and customer complaints).
- Data isolation / compliance requirement: model inputs contain sensitive PII and must not be processed in a multi-tenant pool.
- Current infra complexity: in-house serving on AWS (K8s + autoscaling groups) with manual scaling and significant engineering overhead.

Current stack and constraints:
- Models: two internal instruction-tuned models (Llama-variant) and a smaller reranker.
- Hosting: EC2 G5 instances as spot when available; fall back to on-demand when spot is reclaimed.
- Throughput: baseline 50 requests/sec, peaks ~140 req/sec during batch jobs; average request is ~1.2k tokens.
- Latency SLOs: 95th < 500ms for interactive flows; background batch can tolerate higher latency.
- Security: customer requires SOC2 controls and encryption at rest + KMS for key management.

Success criteria for a Dedicated fit:
1) Predictable throughput with reserved GPU capacity to cover baseline + burst headroom (targeting sustained 60-80 req/sec and 140+ req/sec for 10-15 minute bursts).
2) VPC/private deployment or physical isolation such that customer data does not touch multi-tenant pools.
3) Autoscaling/burst behavior: ability to define burst policy (short lived extra capacity for scheduled batch windows) and guaranteed fallbacks.
4) Cost model: clear monthly reserved price with overage/burst billing and a path to reduce unit costs via batching/cache.

Open technical questions we flagged (action items in parentheses):
- Precise burst profile: duration and frequency of those 140+ req/sec spikes (Alex to share sample traffic histogram).
- Model size + KV cache footprint per GPU (SummitData to confirm model sizes and typical sequence lengths).
- SOC2 evidence timeline and any additional compliance controls required beyond standard KMS/audit logs (Rafael will scope).

Next steps:
1) Alex to share anonymized traffic histogram and model size information - aiming for EOD Thu 2026-07-02. (attachment: summitdata-current-arch.png)
2) I'll send a sizing estimate for a Dedicated pool (reserved GPU count, expected baseline TPS, and burst policy examples) by Monday 2026-07-06. (attachment: sizing-estimate-v1.xlsx)
3) Rafael will follow up separately on SOC2/compliance and provide a short checklist of evidence we can supply.
4) Schedule a technical deep-dive with SummitData infra/ML engineers to validate latency/throughput assumptions - proposed window next week.

If that all looks right I'll draft a mutual action plan and include milestone dates for a pilot. Thanks again - excited to see if Dedicated can simplify your footprint and stabilize costs.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Marissa - thanks for the thorough recap, this matches our notes. A couple clarifications and items from our side:

- We will provide a 48-hour sample traffic histogram and a CSV of request sizes by EOD today (attaching to this thread).
- Model details: primary model ~13B parameters, avg seq length 1,200 tokens; reranker ~2B. KV cache per replica ~4GB.
- Burst windows: typically 10-20 minutes, 3-4x baseline traffic, usually predictable (scheduled nightly enrichment) but occasional customer-driven bursts during day.
- Compliance: SOC2 is in progress; our security team will want to review network diagrams and audit log retention policies.

Two asks from SummitData: 
1) Can Redwood guarantee isolation in Dedicated so that our models and inputs are not colocated with other customers (we need a written assurance for procurement)?
2) If we commit to a 12-month reserved pool, what is the expected uplift in effective throughput / cost per token vs on-demand?

Happy to jump on the tech deep-dive - Sana and I are available Tue/Wed next week PST.

--Alex

- Cost delta: Rough estimate - committing to a 12-month reserved pool typically reduces unit cost 25-40% vs on-demand depending on GPU type and utilization. I'll include a worked example in the sizing sheet.
